To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tribological performance (i.e. wear resistance and friction coefficient) of Si3N₄ composites can be improved by more than twenty and nearly two times, respectively, by addition of FL-GNPs, while preserving the other mechanical properties.
highly wear-resistant and low friction Si3N4 ceramic composites can be achieved by adding graphene nanoplatelets (G-NP) with a very high degree of exfoliation, approaching the 2-D limit.

the addition of FL-GNPs enables the formation of an efficient lubricant tribo-film on the surfaces of the composites, which is at the origin of a significant increase in the wear resistance and reduction in the friction coefficient of the composites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the tribological performance enhancement of Si3N _{4} composites by addition and efficient dispersion of few-layer graphene nanoplatelets.

the development of new materials with improved tribological performance, which are highly promising for applications where low-friction, wear-resistance and thermal stability are required, such as for example in the field of automotive and aerospace industry.

the development of highly efficient and low-cost tribological ceramic composite materials with outstanding wear resistance and low friction coefficient, which are of high interest for a broad variety of industrial applications, such as bearings, gears, cutting tools and machine parts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
by using FL-GNPs in the 2D range, the tribological properties are improved by a factor of up to ten, while the mechanical properties of the composites are preserved or even enhanced.

FL-GNPs are an excellent filler material for improving the tribology of Si3N 4 ceramics, and probably other materials as well, and that the exfoliation of the GNPs to the FL range plays a crucial role in the formation of a tribo-film that can efficiently reduce the friction and wear of the ceramic matrix.
the addition of FL- GNPs to ceramic composites is a very efficient and promising way to significantly improve their tribological properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tribological performance can be significantly enhanced by the addition of FL-GNPs in ceramic materials.
the exfoliation of GNPs down the FL-range is a promising route to achieve highly wear-resistant, low-friction ceramic composites.
the tribological properties can be improved by increasing the exfoliaton degree of graphene nanoplatelet down to the few-layers range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tribological properties and wear resistance of ceramic composites can be significantly improved by using FL-GNP fillers.
the addition of FL-GNPs can be used as a general approach to significantly enhance the tribological properties and wear resistance of ceramic composites.
the tribological properties can be improved by increasing the GNP coverage of surfaces, and that this can be efficiently achieved by reducing the GNP thickness to the FL range.
